title: Dual Form: the m↔n Involution Is One Rewrite
content: qVandermonde_swap produces the dual convolution by exploiting that the binomial argument m+n is symmetric: m+n = n+m (Nat.add_comm), so evaluating the parent identity qVandermonde at the swapped arguments (n, m, r) leaves the left-hand side [m+n choose r]_q unchanged while exchanging the binomial factors and transforming the q-exponent k(m+k−r) ↦ k(n+k−r). No property of the Gaussian binomial beyond the parent identity is used — the symmetry is forced entirely by the symmetry of the argument. This is the q-analog of the manifest m↔n symmetry of the classical Vandermonde sum ∑ₖ C(m,k)C(n,r−k).

title: Two Different-Looking Sums, One Value
content: qVandermonde_sum_symm is the conceptual payload: the original convolution sum and its m↔n swap are equal as ring elements, both computing [m+n choose r]_q. The proof simply chains qVandermonde (rewriting the original sum back to the closed Gaussian binomial via ←) with qVandermonde_swap. What makes this non-trivial is that the equality is invisible term by term: the q-exponents k(m+k−r) and k(n+k−r) differ summand by summand, and only the shared closed value reveals them as the same total. At q=1 this collapses to the obvious classical symmetry; the q-deformation hides it.
prerequisites: transitivity through a common closed form

title: Reflected Index k↦r−k and the Truncated-Subtraction Care
content: qVandermonde_reflect re-indexes the parent sum by the involution k ↦ r−k on Finset.range (r+1), supplied cleanly by Finset.sum_range_reflect (which maps k ↦ (r+1)−1−k = r−k). The resulting q-exponent takes the dual shape (r−k)(m−k) with the binomial factors index-reflected. The only subtlety is truncated natural-number subtraction: for in-range indices k ≤ r one needs r−(r−k)=k, m+(r−k)−r=m−k, and (r+1)−1−k=r−k. All three are discharged by omega after extracting k ≤ r from membership (Nat.lt_succ_iff), then rewritten with simp. This is the q-analog of the classical k↦r−k reflection symmetry of the Vandermonde sum.
prerequisites: reflection of a finite summation range

title: The Reflected Sum Equals the Original
content: qVandermonde_reflect_sum_symm completes the picture: the original convolution sum and its k↦r−k reflection are equal ring elements, again via the shared value [m+n choose r]_q (chain ←qVandermonde with qVandermonde_reflect). Together with qVandermonde_sum_symm this records, as machine-checked statements, both involutive symmetries (factor-swap and index-reflection) that the single algebraic form of the q-Vandermonde identity obscures — the two generators of a dihedral action on the family of equivalent q-weighted sums, as noted in the entry's open questions.
prerequisites: transitivity through a common closed form
